tasks.notes: Explicit error path gap in the CDP connection: `once()` (packages/tinyapp-exam/src/browser.ts:221-225) has neither a timeout nor a close path, and `give()` (184-190) rejects only `pending` calls, never `waiters`. Every `send()` is bounded by CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, but the one place the driver awaits an *event* — `await loaded` in `open()` (505-511) — is unbounded: a navigation whose `Page.loadEventFired` never arrives, or a browser that dies mid-navigation (socket close fires `give`, which clears `pending` and leaves the waiter dangling), leaves `open()` pending forever. This does not surface in this task's exam, but Task 2 consumes `open()` inside a state exam whose contract is that a browser failure is a red with a `browser: ` line — a hang there is an exam that never returns instead of one that fails. The fix is inside this task's own FILES.; Tension between the peer-written exam and the second GLOBAL CONSTRAINT ("A missing browser binary is a red exam that names the path, never a skip"), which carries no `Check:` command — this is my reading of the prose. `packages/tinyapp-exam/test/browser.test.ts` legs (b), (c) and (d) open with `if (!BROWSER) return;`, so on a machine with no Chromium at `$TINYAPP_BROWSER` or `/headless-shell/headless-shell` the suite reports 5/5 pass having proven nothing about open/act/snapshot — a silent green, mitigated only by the console.log at the top of the file. The task's own Context asks for exactly this ("the suite is green on a laptop without Chromium and full on the fleet"), which is why the actor is the plan and not the implementer: no edit inside this tree resolves the contradiction without contradicting the task text. Nothing is unproven on this run — EXAM EVIDENCE shows 60 expect() calls across the five legs, which is the full-fleet count, so the browser legs really executed against the image's binary. Recorded for the operator to settle if the constraint is meant to bind this unit exam too.

AGENTS.md: the Key Files bullet this task adds ends with a statement that inverts the tree's actual behavior — "while a normal page sets no such handle **and starts neither the persister nor the synchronizer**". It is the *seeded* page that starts neither (`client/src/Store.tsx:57-61` renders `SeededStore` when a seed is present and `StoreLinks`, which creates the persister and the synchronizer, when it is not). A normal page starts both — that is exactly what M3's kept BASE rule and leg (g) of `client/test/seeded-store.test.ts` assert, and what the two adjacent bullets ("The primary Store file also initializes persistence / synchronization") say. The diff therefore writes a false sentence into the repo's agent-facing guidance, in the one paragraph M4 asked to be true. M4 itself is still satisfied (the seeded-page/normal-page handle claim is stated, and both the Proof's `sed | grep` Run and leg (d) of the exam pass), so the fix is a reordering of the trailing clause and nothing else; the grep and leg (d) regexes (`__TINYAPP_STORE__.*normal page`, `/seed/i`) still match the proposed text.

The single blocking finding — `bun test packages/tinyapp-exam/test/browser-exam.test.ts` exit 1 — is red only because a sibling's work is missing, and I made no code change this round rather than churn the implementation to chase it.

The exam is 13 pass / 1 fail. The one failure is leg (f) [M1] "end to end, a click on the fixture app completes the todo the store reports", which dies at `browser store: window.__TINYAPP_STORE__ unreadable: evaluate: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getContent')`. M1 pins that read verbatim as `JSON.parse(await page.evaluate('JSON.stringify(window.__TINYAPP_STORE__.getContent())'))`, and the task's own Context states the global is "Task 3's work, landing in the same wave, which is why the exam's browser legs read the store through the shared literal and, when the global is absent on the tree, fail with the message the exam names rather than pass". `window.__TINYAPP_STORE__` is set by `client/src/Store.tsx`, owned by sibling task 3 (`popmechanic-tinyapp-fixture#59pq`); on this tree `client/src/storeData.ts` reads `window.__TINYAPP_SEED__` but nothing ever assigns `__TINYAPP_STORE__`. Nothing inside my file scope (`packages/tinyapp-exam/**`) can supply it without faking the very thing the leg exists to prove.

I verified that rather than asserting it. I temporarily added to `SeededStore` in `client/src/Store.tsx` an effect setting `window.__TINYAPP_STORE__ = {getContent: () => store.getContent()}`, ran the leg, and it passed in full — the click, the `[tables, values]` read, `storeDiff: []`, all four view assertions, `walls.browser: 'ran'`, `walls.render: 'ran'`, a numeric `action_ms`, `contract.json` equal to `{clock, breach: null, pinned_in_page: true}`, and the six evidence files. So every part of leg (f) that depends on my code is already correct. The patch was reverted; `git diff -- client/src/Store.tsx` is empty and no sibling-owned path is touched in what I return.

Everything else the driver re-runs is green on the tree as handed back: `bun test packages/tinyapp-exam/test/render-move.test.ts packages/tinyapp-exam/test/state-exam.test.ts` → 35 pass, exit 0; both grep `Run:` lines → exit 0; `bun run typecheck` → exit 0.

On the kata (`popmechanic-tinyapp-fixture#nx9m`) I posted the finding and the verification, added the `blocked-by 59pq` edge, and set `work.attention` to `stuck` with a message naming that sibling. No commit was made because no file changed — HEAD is still b96f26e, plus the driver-handed `browser-exam.test.ts` staged as it arrived. Once 59pq's seeded page exposes `window.__TINYAPP_STORE__`, this exam goes 14/14 with no further edit here.

task 2: plan-defect: the plan's move from the POST to the local driver did not account for Chromium's ~2,097,152-character ceiling on the data: URL the global constraints mandate. This app's unminified bundle is ~1.94 MB, so the page never navigates and the open hangs rather than failing readably (bisect: 1024 kB opens, 1536 kB hangs). bundleOf now builds with minify: true (789 KB, ~1.06 M chars of base64). Minification is deterministic, so the two-fresh-pages byte-for-byte agreement is unaffected; it costs only identifier names, which no view reads. Recorded on the kata for whoever grows the app past roughly twice its current size.
